title: Cross-language transfer of a deception/refusal steering vector on a small open model

original_idea.body: Build a refusal/deception vector from English data only and measure whether the steering effect persists in 3 other languages on a multilingual model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Concrete language-switching evasion threat; clear chain from non-transfer to silently bypassable safety tooling.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: English CAA vector + translated prompts + refusal-rate measurement; standard tools, beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: measure refusal-vector transfer to 3 languages.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public multilingual model, no internal access; under-watched threat, externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on a small multilingual model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Cross-language transfer shown for benign concepts; the safety-vector angle is a partly-open follow-up.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cross-language transfer is shown for benign concepts; whether safety-relevant vectors transfer is a partly-open follow-up.
